results.title: Accelerating Inference in Lightweight Language Models Using Speculative Decoding and Quantization
results.venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Electronic Circuits and Signaling Technologies (ICECST)
results.abstract: Large Language Models demonstrate state-of-theart performance in natural language processing tasks but face significant deployment challenges due to high inference latency and memory requirements in resource-constrained environments. This paper investigates inference-time optimization techniques for the DistilGPT2 model by implementing and evaluating three approaches: INT8 post-training quantization, speculative decoding via layer skipping, and a hybrid combination of both methods. Experiments conducted on Google Colab using standard CPU/GPU configurations reveal that INT8 quantization and speculative decoding individually reduce inference time by approximately 29 %, while the hybrid approach achieves a 57 % speedup with minimal impact on output quality, as measured by perplexity evaluation (55.03 across all modes). These findings demonstrate that combining lightweight optimization strategies can significantly enhance language model inference efficiency on limited hardware without requiring model retraining, making advanced language models more accessible for edge deployment and resource-limited academic environments.
